results.label: this tree ships the zone-method vocabulary and the consolidation walk (src/bots/smc.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
a new account has made no choice at all: the setting is absent rather than defaulted to a value it never picked
an analysis with no choice made runs the pivot method, and says nobody chose rather than claiming it was asked for
every zone it plotted is the pivot candle with no consolidation walk attached
and the filter publishes the whole closed vocabulary, so a client can render the choice it is offering
`?zone_method=range` really plots the consolidation: the method, the source of the choice and the applied count all say range
and every origin the two runs BOTH plot is a superset: the range box contains the pivot box, box by box
each range zone carries the walk that produced it (bars, width in ATR, what stopped it)
the request is not stored by asking: one request cannot rewrite the trader’s preference
the choice is saved through the app’s own settings route and reported back
and it is the trader’s row, not a process-wide default: the next request reads it back
an analysis that asks for NOTHING now runs the range method: the stored choice is consulted, not merely echoed
and it is the same geometry the explicit request produced
another account is not affected by this one’s choice: the preference is per user, not a process-wide default
an explicit `?zone_method=pivot` overrides the stored range for that request, so both methods can be tested side by side
and that single request did not move the stored choice
the vocabulary is folded, not taken literally: a padded, upper-case request is the range method
a method this app cannot plot runs the pivot geometry and NAMES the request and the vocabulary on the payload
and the zones really are the pivot boxes, so the sentence and the picture agree
saving a method this app cannot plot is REFUSED by name rather than quietly ignored
and a refused save leaves the stored choice exactly as it was
the choice can be released back to the default (empty clears it, and the analysis says asked-nothing again)
the chart draws the same geometry the analysis used (M124: the chart is not a second opinion)
and every zone the chart DOES draw names its own geometry: range where the consolidation was walked, pivot with the reason where it could not be
a scan row carries the method it was built with, so a list of markets can never be read on an unnamed geometry
an incoming TradingView alert is analysed with the trader’s own zone method, and the verdict carries it
and the STORED alert history names the geometry too, so an unattended verdict can be attributed later without re-running it
reading the range geometry writes exactly what reading the pivot geometry writes — a method adds no row of its own
and the milestone adds NO table, index, trigger or column of its own: the choice lives in the settings JSON the app already stores

scope: M30 api: the zone-method choice over the real routes, its ownership and its read-only proof: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
